origin_region: Southern Province · Galle, Matara and Deniyaya (sea level to 600 m)
cultivar: Assam-type seedling bushes and TRI clones
processing: Fully oxidised orthodox black tea; the warm, wet south grows big, fast leaf that is rolled heavily into long, wiry leaf grades (OP, OP1, FBOP, Pekoe) and extra-tippy grades rather than the broken grades of the hills.
harvest_season: Year-round with little seasonal swing; the first and last quarters are a touch brighter.
appearance_dry: Long, black, wiry twisted leaf (OP1) or chunky Pekoe, often with golden tips (FBOP).
appearance_liquor: Dark red-brown to deep copper, strong-looking.
taste_profile: Strong, thick and sweet: malt, dark caramel and a faint smoky or honey note, low in briskness, built for milk or for the Middle Eastern strong-tea market.

brewing.notes: Boiling water, four minutes, milk or sugar optional; leaf grades stand a second steep.

vintage_note: Sold weekly through the Colombo auction by factory and leaf grade; 'low-grown' is the trade's shorthand for the style, and OP1, FBOP and Pekoe from southern factories are the grades to look for, much of it packed for export to the Gulf, Iran and Russia. Quality is even through the year and the tea keeps a year or two sealed.
description:
Ruhuna is the low country of southern Sri Lanka, the wet, warm hills behind Galle, Matara and Deniyaya that rise from near sea level to about 600 metres. It is the newest of the island's big tea districts, mostly smallholder land feeding private factories, and it makes a style of Ceylon tea that is the opposite of the pale high-grown cups: dark, strong, sweet and built for the strong-tea markets of the Middle East and Russia.

The warm, humid climate grows large leaf fast, and the factories make the most of it with heavy orthodox rolling into long, wiry, black leaf grades (OP1, Pekoe, FBOP) and extra-tippy grades, rather than the broken grades of the hills. Low-grown leaf also has a different balance of polyphenols, which gives the dark, thick, low-astringency cup.

Expect a deep red-brown liquor with malt, dark caramel and honey, a faint smoky or sweet-tobacco edge in some lots, and surprisingly little briskness for a tea this strong. Brew it with boiling water for four minutes, with milk or sugar if you like; the leaf grades will stand a second steep.

It is sold weekly through the Colombo auction by factory and leaf grade, and 'low-grown' is the trade's shorthand for the style; OP1, FBOP and Pekoe grades from southern factories are what to look for, often packed for export to Dubai, Tehran and Moscow. Quality is even through the year, and the tea keeps for a year or two sealed.

If you find the hill Ceylons thin, this is the district for you; it is also the base of most Ceylon teas sold in the Gulf.
